en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Rolling Together (Tuvaṭṭavagga) 32. The Training Rule on Rolling Together on a Single Blanket.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were lying down two together on a single bed-cover and upper garment.
People, while wandering on a tour of the monastery, saw them and complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs lie down two together on a single bed-cover and upper garment, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can these bhikkhunīs lie down together, sharing one blanket and one upper robe?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that nuns are lying down on two [mats] with a single coverlet and upper cloth?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
“How indeed, monks, can nuns lie down using two [robes] as a single covering?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:”
“Whatever nuns should lie down together on a single bed-cover and a single upper garment, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nuns” means whichever such [nuns]... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunīs" refers to those who are fully ordained (upasampannā).
"Two [nuns] should lie down on one bed and one coverlet" means...
If they spread out that very same [blanket] and put on that very same [cloak], it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If there is one blanket and one cloak, and they lie down while perceiving them as one blanket and one cloak, it is an offense of expiation.
If there is one blanket and one cloak, and they lie down while being doubtful about them, it is an offense of expiation.
If there is one spread and one coverlet, but they perceive them as different spreads and different coverlets, they lie down together; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If there is one spread and different coverlets, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If there are different spreads and one coverlet, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is a separate rug and cloak, and she perceives them as a single rug and cloak, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is a separate rug and cloak, and she is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is a separate rug and cloak, and she perceives them as separate rugs and cloaks, there is no offense.
There is no offense if they lie down after having indicated a boundary,
or if they are insane.
"For those who are first offenders.
The second training rule is concluded.
